title: Disney’s new Star Wars animatronics interact with guests using AI
slides: Can Disney's Star Wars robots outsmart park guests?
New animatronics react in real time, not scripted loops.
They listen, respond, and remember your name — unsettlingly well.
Expect longer queues as guests stall to test the machines.
Watch one interaction closely — then ask who's really performing.
thread_text:
1. Would You Work For This Robot?

Disney's new Star Wars animatronics don't run on loops. They listen, respond, and remember your name — and guests are lining up to test them.

2. Real-Time Reactions

These machines track voices and gestures live, not from a script. The park becomes a stage where the audience is the scene partner.

3. The Unsettling Part

They recall your name from earlier in the day. That's not a canned loop — that's a memory system built to make you feel seen.

4. Queues as a Consequence

Guests stall interactions to see how smart the bots get. Wait times climb while everyone tries to outsmart a machine that's already learning.

5. The Real Question

Watch one interaction this week and ask: who's performing — the robot, or you? If you can't tell, the line worked.
